Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Janet Morales (Redwood AE), Marco Ibarra (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (CISO, Avalon), Evan Holt (Procurement), Dr. Lena Ortiz (IT Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
Quick walkthrough of Avalon Health vendor risk questionnaire focused on SIG/CAIQ items. Primary topics: SOC 2 evidence, SSO/RBAC controls, audit log retention and exportability, KMS key ownership and BYOK options, and data residency for patient data. Action items include sending SOC2 and SIG mapping, scheduling a KMS deep-dive, and confirming data residency requirements.

Transcript:
[00:00] Janet Morales: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Janet from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on the account. With me is Marco, our solutions engineer. Can you, uh, do quick intros?
[00:07] Marco Ibarra: Hey all, Marco here. I focus on private deployments and security integrations, happy to dig into KMS and audit trails.
[00:12] Priya Desai: Hi, Priya here, chief information security officer at Avalon Health. Evan from procurement and Lena from compliance are on as well. Thanks for making time.
[00:20] Evan Holt: Thanks.
[00:22] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Hi, everyone.
[00:24] Janet Morales: Great. Goal for today is to walk the vendor-assurance questionnaire you sent, mainly the SIG and CAIQ sections you flagged, and agree on what evidence we can hand you and what needs a technical deep dive. Does that sound right, Priya?
[00:36] Priya Desai: Yes, that's it. We have a number of high-priority items: SOC 2 Type II confirmation, encryption and KMS, SSO and RBAC, audit-logging, and obviously data residency for PHI. We'll also want a rough timeline for evidence delivery.
[00:49] Marco Ibarra: Cool. I'll jump in on the technical bits. Quick note up front: Redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private VPC options. For HIPAA-like constraints most customers go dedicated or private; we can call out exactly what evidence maps to each.
[01:03] Janet Morales: I'll share the mapping doc after and link the SOC 2 attestation. Marco, maybe start on SSO/RBAC?
[01:10] Marco Ibarra: Sure. On SSO we support SAML 2.0 with IdPs such as Okta, Azure AD, Ping. We also support SCIM for user provisioning. For RBAC we have role-based policies at the org, project, and route levels — i.e., token scoping and per-model permissions.
[01:27] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Can you spell out what 'route-level' means? We need to know if a user can be prevented from calling certain models that might have PHI exposure.
[01:36] Marco Ibarra: Right. Route-level means you can create an API route that only allows access to certain model versions or inference types. So you can set an allow list; for example production routes that handle PHI can be locked down to private deployment clusters only. There's also audit hooks on every request.
[01:50] Priya Desai: Audit hooks — are they immutable? Our legal team will want non-repudiation and retention controls, maybe WORM storage.
[01:59] Marco Ibarra: We emit structured audit logs (JSON) to your chosen sinks: S3, GCS, or a syslog/ELK stack. Current retention by default is 90 days on hosted, but for Dedicated/Private you can set retention policies and ship to your own bucket with lifecycle rules, including WORM if your storage supports it.
[02:17] Evan Holt: Will we get a sample export? Procurement wants to see the format.
[02:21] Janet Morales: Yes — we'll attach a sample log export after this call. Note: it's typically timestamp, user id, route id, model id, token usage, and a request hash. The request and response bodies are redacted by default unless you enable request-body logging for a route.
[02:38] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Request-body redaction — is that automatic, or configurable? We can't log PHI in payloads.
[02:45] Marco Ibarra: Default is redact. You can opt in for debug but it's an explicit flag and we'd recommend against storing PHI in those logs. For private deployments you can enable a local-only debug store but it's an admin action and we document consent flows.
[02:59] Priya Desai: Okay. Next up, SOC 2 and ISO. We need to see last SOC 2 Type II report and the scope — alpha systems, does inference runtime fall in scope?
[03:12] Janet Morales: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II certified — we'll share the attestation. The scope includes control plane, "hosted inference", and our observability pipelines; Dedicated customer-managed compute runs outside our shared environment and evidence differs — we'll map that too.
[03:28] Priya Desai: When you say "hosted inference" is in scope, that implies your keys and KMS live in Redwood. Does Redwood hold customer keys?
[03:36] Marco Ibarra: For hosted, Redwood manages encryption at rest keys, but we offer a customer-managed KMS integration for Dedicated and Private — BYOK via AWS KMS (Customer master key), GCP CMEK, or Azure Key Vault. We can provide evidence of key separation and HSM-backed KMS for those.
[03:53] Evan Holt: If we go dedicated but still want Redwood to operate patches, do we get access to the KMS? Who rotates keys?
[03:59] Marco Ibarra: In a typical Dedicated model you can choose either Redwood-managed keys or BYOK. If BYOK, your security team controls rotation. We can support automatic rotation hooks, but rotation events are logged and you retain control.
[04:11] Dr. Lena Ortiz: We need proof of key lifecycle policy and documented rotations for audit.
[04:15] Janet Morales: We'll include a KMS lifecycle doc and example rotation logs.
[04:19] [00:04:19] Priya Desai: How about encryption in transit? TLS only? Any mTLS options?
[04:24] Marco Ibarra: TLS 1.2+ for control plane and data in transit. For private deployments we support mTLS between internal services and can enable client certificate verification for inbound routes.
[04:34] Janet Morales: Also we can provide network diagrams and flowcharts showing control plane vs data plane and where encryption boundaries are.
[04:40] Evan Holt: Good. On data residency — Avalon holds patient PII — we need to lock data to US regions, ideally east and central. Is that possible on hosted?
[04:50] Marco Ibarra: Hosted has region constraints — we currently offer US, EU, and APAC regions. For strict residency you should look at Dedicated or Private. With Dedicated we can provision capacity in a specific region and ensure logs and models are pinned. For Private (VPC or on-prem) you, the customer, retain full control of where data resides.
[05:06] Priya Desai: What's the difference between Dedicated and Private from an evidence POV?
[05:11] Marco Ibarra: Dedicated is Redwood-hosted hardware dedicated to you but the control plane is still Redwood-managed — so some control plane telemetry is in scope of our SOC 2. Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane (we provide an appliance or VPC template), which shifts many controls to your responsibility. We'll map each SIG item to the appropriate deployment model.
[05:29] Janet Morales: We'll make a table showing evidence for hosted vs dedicated vs private for every SIG line item.
[05:34] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Perfect. The procurement form also asks about penetration testing cadence and whether Redwood shares pentest result summaries.
[05:41] Marco Ibarra: We do annual external pentests plus periodic red-team exercises. We can provide summary findings and remediation notes; detailed raw reports are usually shared under NDA.
[05:50] Priya Desai: NDA is fine.
[05:52] Evan Holt: Also question about data deletion and ML model training: do you train on customer prompts? Is any customer data used to fine-tune models?
[05:59] Marco Ibarra: Short answer: no for hosted by default — we don't use customer data to train Redwood-verified models. For customers who explicitly opt-in to analytics or fine-tuning we have an agreement flow and data is isolated. We'll add contractual language and examples.
[06:13] Priya Desai: Need to see that language for procurement.
[06:17] Janet Morales: We'll attach a sample data processing addendum and opt-in contract language.
[06:21] [00:06:21] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Audit retention — you mentioned 90 days default for hosted. For us, legal wants 7 years for some logs — do you support long-term archival?
[06:31] Marco Ibarra: Yes, for Dedicated/Private you can ship to your own archival bucket with lifecycle policies to keep 7 years. For hosted we can, under an enterprise agreement, configure extended retention and export. We'll note the cost delta.
[06:44] Priya Desai: Can you produce proof of tamper resistance for those exported logs? We use WORM + object lock for certain datasets.
[06:50] Marco Ibarra: If you export to your own S3 with object lock enabled, that provides WORM. Redwood cannot bypass your bucket's object lock. For hosted-managed archives we can enable S3 Object Lock in compliance mode but that requires a contract change — we'll show both patterns.
[07:05] Evan Holt: On the SIG spreadsheet, item A.2.1 asks about 'logical access reviews' — what cadence does Redwood use?
[07:12] Janet Morales: Quarterly logical access reviews for internal users, and customer-facing RBAC audit can be done on request. We'll include the policy doc and a sample audit log that shows admin role changes.
[07:23] Priya Desai: Great. A security engineer question — how do you handle key-value cache in inference? For example KV cache persistence across sessions.
[07:33] Marco Ibarra: There might be a small transcription mismatch there — but yes, the KV cache (we call it K-V cache) is ephemeral per request unless you enable session persistence. If persistence is enabled in private deployments, the cache is stored in your cluster, and we can show lifecycle and purge controls. For hosted ephemeral caches are purged after session expiry and not written to durable storage.
[07:52] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Are there documented retention timers and APIs to trigger cache purging?
[07:57] Marco Ibarra: Yes — API to invalidate caches and TTL settings. We'll link the admin API docs.
[08:02] Janet Morales: We're seeing a few procurement-specific asks in the spreadsheet about insurance and liability caps. Those are legal questions, i'll follow up with sales ops.
[08:10] Evan Holt: Sounds good. Back to KMS — auditor wants to see proof of HSM-backed keys. Can you provide that?
[08:16] Marco Ibarra: For our managed keys we use AWS KMS with HSM under the hood; for dedicated/private using customer KMS you can produce the provider's HSM attestation. We'll attach the relevant vendor docs and an example KMS access policy.
[08:29] Priya Desai: Alright. A few SIG items reference multi-tenancy isolation and noisy-neighbor risks. Can you provide isolation guarantees?
[08:38] Marco Ibarra: Dedicated yields tenancy isolation at the hardware level, private is fully single-tenant. For hosted we use tenant isolation via containers and strict cgroups plus network policies — we can provide architecture diagrams and our performance isolation metrics. We also have guardrails like per-tenant QC limits and fallback routing to prevent noisy neighbor from impacting other customers.
[08:59] Priya Desai: We'll need the perf isolation data for the vendor risk team.
[09:03] Marco Ibarra: We'll include the perf baseline report and how we model SLOs.
[09:08] Janet Morales: Question from procurement: who is the subprocessor list?
[09:12] Evan Holt: yes, we need specific names for our procurement clause.
[09:15] Marco Ibarra: Subprocessors include cloud providers (AWS, GCP), CDNs, monitoring vendors, and a small set of managed infra partners; we'll attach the latest subprocessor list and update cadence.
[09:26] Priya Desai: Can you confirm whether any subprocessors have access to plaintext request payloads?
[09:31] Marco Ibarra: No. We have strict controls; plaintext payloads are not shared with subprocessors. If debug logging is enabled it can be routed but that requires customer consent and is auditable.
[09:43] Dr. Lena Ortiz: On evidence labeling — procurement likes to see a single ZIP with CSV index mapping each SIG question to a document or screenshot. Can Redwood produce that?
[09:53] Janet Morales: Absolutely. We'll prepare the SIG mapping CSV plus the artifacts: network diagrams, SOC2 attestation, KMS lifecycle example, audit-log sample, SSO configs, pentest summary.
[10:03] Priya Desai: We'll want the CSV to also flag items that need NDA for full reports.
[10:09] Janet Morales: We'll flag them.
[10:11] [00:10:11] Evan Holt: A quick question: license and model weights — if we bring our own model artifacts will Redwood host them? And what's the control plane visibility?
[10:19] Marco Ibarra: You can bring your own model artifacts on Dedicated or Private. The serving runtime treats them as customer-supplied; model weights are stored in customer-controlled buckets if BYO. We can also attest that weights are not accessible outside that tenant.
[10:33] Priya Desai: Another compliance item: do you support SSO session timeouts and device compliance checks?
[10:38] Marco Ibarra: We respect IdP session timeouts and can enforce inactivity timeouts on the control plane. For device posture we integrate with IdP signals but don't do endpoint posture checks by default — you can combine with a CASB.
[10:51] Dr. Lena Ortiz: For legal, we need data flow diagrams showing PHI never leaves specified region.
[10:56] Janet Morales: We'll produce a region-specific data flow diagram for the US-east deployment model.
[10:59] Priya Desai: Good. What's the typical timeline to gather all artifacts? We need them for our vendor committee next week.
[11:07] Janet Morales: We can assemble a SIG mapping and the non-NDA docs in 2 business days; SOC 2 is an attestation we can share immediately, pentest summaries under NDA in 2-3 days, and a KMS deep-dive needs SE time, so maybe schedule for next week.
[11:22] Evan Holt: Ok that timing works; procurement wants final bundle by 2026-03-23 if possible.
[11:28] Priya Desai: That would be helpful.
[11:30] Marco Ibarra: I'll block a deep-dive slot tentatively next Wednesday, 2026-03-25, unless you prefer earlier.
[11:38] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Next Wednesday works for our security team.
[11:41] Janet Morales: Great. Any other high-risk items we haven't covered?
[11:45] Priya Desai: One last thing — legal asks about breach notification SLAs and forensics support.
[11:50] Marco Ibarra: Our incident response policy includes 24-hour initial notification for incidents affecting confidentiality and we provide forensic artifacts as part of our IR playbook. We'll attach the IR summary and escalation contacts.
[12:01] Priya Desai: Please include RACI for incident handling so we can insert it in the procurement binder.
[12:08] Janet Morales: Will do.
[12:11] [00:12:11] Evan Holt: Any cost delta numbers for longer log retention and BYOK? Procurement wants ballpark figures.
[12:18] Marco Ibarra: We typically provide a sizing worksheet — longer retention is mostly storage cost plus ingestion fee; BYOK has an operational fee. We'll add a preliminary estimate in the bundle.
[12:29] Priya Desai: One nit: in the SIG spreadsheet item about 'evidence of encryption in transit' who signs off that it's in scope — us or you?
[12:37] Janet Morales: We'll provide the technical evidence; your auditor signs off on whether it meets your policy. We'll note that in the mapping CSV.
[12:45] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Ok.
[12:46] Janet Morales: Quick recap of action items — I'll read them out: 1) Redwood to upload SIG mapping CSV and attach SOC2 attestation and non-NDA docs by 2026-03-20. 2) Marco to run and share a small private-deploy perf benchmark and KMS examples by 2026-03-25. 3) Priya to confirm residency and procurement form by 2026-03-22. Any corrections?
[13:07] Priya Desai: That matches our notes.
[13:09] Evan Holt: Yep.
[13:10] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Good.
[13:11] Janet Morales: Great, i'll send calendar invites for the deep dive and share the bundle link when ready. Thanks everyone.
[13:16] Priya Desai: Thanks.
